plan.architecture:
Option B, as chosen: one Cargo workspace containing a Rust core library, a clap CLI over it, and a Tauri 2 app that links the same library. The upstream solvers run unchanged, as child processes. lib_interface is used only as a CI oracle and is never shipped.

DATA FLOW (every arrow is a typed Result with a reason code; no stage downgrades a failure to a warning):
project.json (f64 world metres, Z-up, stable UUIDs, one declared band set)
 -> validate (every pre-launch rule in the contract survey)
 -> .cbin + .poly (facet marker = scene face index, max_digits10)
 -> tetgen.exe (child process in a Job Object)
 -> TetGen reader. Markers come from .face. Any exit != 0, *_skipped.face or missing .neigh is a FAIL.
 -> .mbin builder (face order b,d,c / c,d,a / a,d,b / b,c,a; idVolume mapped explicitly; invariants checked; sha256-linked to its .cbin)
 -> config.xml, generated from the schema
 -> spps.exe / classicalTheory.exe. cwd = a fresh dated run folder and the argument is 'config.xml', which works around the narrow-path failure verified with 'Ł'.
 -> run verification: every stdout and stderr line is classified by content; the stats GABE is read; expected files are checked; exit semantics are judged per solver.
 -> readers -> our own per-band parameters -> UI.

A run is OK only when the exit semantics, the line classification, the per-band particle statistics and the expected-file check all agree. [verified] SPPS exits 0 on unreadable meshes, on 100% particle loss and when trans_epsilon is missing, and crashes with 0xC0000005 when a source is outside the mesh or material 0 is missing (contract survey run_* folders). So no single signal is trusted.

CRATES
- `core` (lib): schema, validation, geometry import/check/repair, meshing behind a `Mesher` trait (first backend: tetgen.exe), clean-room codecs written from docs/formats, the run manager, result readers, parameters, and the physics bed with its analytic references.
- `cli` (clap): every core operation, with JSON output and stable exit codes: 0 OK, 2 validation, 3 geometry, 4 mesh, 5 solver run, 6 result verification, 130 cancelled. Every milestone gate before the GUI is a CLI invocation, so the core is proven before a window exists.
- `app` (Tauri >= 2.11.6): links `core` and exposes async commands only. Run events travel over an ipc::Channel batched at about 50 ms. Decoded datasets travel as ipc::Response raw bytes. Virtual-host mapping is the fallback, chosen by a benchmark on Grace.
- The webview gets no shell or fs permission. All WebView2-specific code sits in one module, which is where the Tauri v3 migration will touch.

SOLVERS
- spps, classicalTheory and tetgen are built from `git archive 929a5c8` into a build directory on D:. B:\repos\I-Simpa-upstream is never written to.
- patches/ exists but stays empty, because the decision is to run the solvers unchanged.
- A solver manifest (sha256 of each exe plus build flags) is recorded in every run.
- No lib_interface code runs in any shipped binary.

ORACLES (CI only)
- oracle/ is a C++ probe built from the 9-file Boost-free lib_interface subset, which the survey verified builds and round-trips the upstream fixtures. It diffs every Rust writer's output and every reader's decode.
- The solver is the final oracle: 0 'Xml Property ... doesn't exist !' lines, and per-band loss taken from the stats GABE.

CRASH ISOLATION
- panic=unwind; command bodies wrapped in catch_unwind; every allocation bounded by the file length.
- unsafe Win32 code is confined to one `winproc` module (Job Object with KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE, CREATE_NO_WINDOW).
- Contingency: a `cli serve` mode (option E) if an in-process panic is ever seen to close the window.

LICENCE POSTURE
- GPL-3 now.
- The core is written clean-room from a spec. The solvers and TetGen are separate executables talking through files and a command line (an aggregate in the FSF FAQ's sense).
- The `Mesher` trait keeps fTetWild (MPL-2.0) or a WIAS-licensed TetGen reachable, so a commercial version is not foreclosed. Whether this is enough is a legal question, not an engineering one.

PHYSICS BEFORE PIXELS: no acoustic number appears in the GUI until the shoebox bed (M8) passes, and any parameter without a passing bed is hidden.

components.name: core::schema
components.responsibility: Typed project model. serde for persistence, schemars for the JSON Schema used by CLI validation and UI forms, ts-rs for the TypeScript types. Uses f64 world metres (Z-up), UUID ids that never reach the solver as counters, and one band set that every source, material and fitting zone must carry. Material reflection laws are an enum bound by name to the solver codes: 0 specular, 1 uniform, 2 Lambert (coreTypes.h:84-92). The project file is versioned JSON whose floats round-trip bit-exactly. Undo is built from operations with inverses, so it can be tested without a screen.

components.name: core::validate
components.responsibility:
Pre-launch rules, each with a reason code listed in docs/solver-contract.md:
- the same band set on freq_enum and on every source, material and fitting zone, with no duplicate frequencies
- docalc written as the literal '1'
- material 0 defined whenever a face uses it, and every idMat, idRs and idEn declared
- sources and receivers strictly inside the volume and off every face
- type-5 directivity files parsed: 38 fields per row, phi in 5-degree steps
- trans_epsilon present, rayon_recepteurp > 0 and pasdetemps > 0
- duree/pasdetemps below 65,536 steps
- names and labels under 50 bytes, safe as file names and unique
- no zero-length direction vectors
- alpha = 1 forces diffusion to 0; tau <= alpha is corrected, with a warning
- absatmo given in explicit units (the solver reads it as 1/m energy attenuation)

components.name: core::geometry
components.responsibility:
Importers:
- PLY: ASCII, binary little- and big-endian, layer_id plus layer names
- OBJ: g and usemtl groups
- STL: consistent vertex welding
- upstream .proj, read-only: sceneMesh.bin v1.2 with the record size taken from the node span, .finfo groups, idmat, and <position> children for sources and receivers

Units and up axis are explicit import options and are never guessed.

Check: an edge-use census for open and non-manifold edges, degenerate and duplicate faces, orientation and signed volume, and self-intersections found with a BVH and exact predicates. It reports at face level.

Repair: welding, removal of degenerate and duplicate faces, and orientation unification, each change logged. Holes and self-intersections are refused with a reason. Re-import keeps material assignments by matching face centres within a tolerance.

components.name: core::mesh
components.responsibility:
A `Mesher` trait, with tetgen.exe as its first backend.
- .poly writer: facet markers '1 0 <faceIndex>', max_digits10, classic number formatting, and a region list for fitting zones.
- Mesh flags are recorded in the run manifest.
- Failure: an exit other than 0, a *_skipped.face file or a missing .neigh is a FAIL. Skipped markers are mapped back to scene faces and groups, then TetGen -d runs for detail.
- .mbin builder: markers taken from .face (not from matching vertices), neighbour -1 becomes -2, idVolume set explicitly (room 0, fitting region = fitting id). There is no neighbour fallback.
- Invariants checked before writing: 0 degenerate tets, 0 boundary faces with neighbour < 0 and marker -1, every scene face covered, every index in range.
- A manifest links sha256(.cbin) to sha256(.mbin).
- Stale outputs are deleted before every mesh.

components.name: core::formats
components.responsibility:
Clean-room codecs written only from docs/formats.
- Writers: .cbin, .mbin, .poly, config.xml.
- Readers: .cbin, .mbin, TetGen .node/.ele/.face/.neigh/_skipped.face, GABE v2, .csbin (honouring the stored struct lengths 264/16/8), .pbin (honouring the stored lengths, with platform-sized header fields).
- Every reader checks version and length, bounds each allocation by the file size, and returns a typed error. None of them panics.

components.name: core::run
components.responsibility:
Process layer:
- tokio::process launches each child in a Job Object with KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE and CREATE_NO_WINDOW.
- stdout and stderr are read concurrently. Each line is tagged with its stream and a timestamp, split on \n or \r, and a trailing partial line is flushed at EOF.
- Cancel is recorded explicitly as 'cancelled'.

Solver layer:
- Each run gets a fresh dated folder; cwd is set to it and the argument is 'config.xml'.
- A content classifier driven by a table maps lines to FAIL / WARN / INFO / OK / PROGRESS. 'Xml Property' lines count as FAIL.
- Exit semantics are judged per solver. SPPS exit 0 is not success, 0xC0000005 is CRASH, and TCR returns real codes.
- Post-run checks read the stats GABE per band, require total = nbparticules x computed bands, and require the expected files to exist and be non-empty.
- A run manifest records the input hashes, solver hashes, app version, flags, status and reason codes.

components.name: core::results + core::params
components.responsibility:
Assembles typed RunResults only from runs that passed verification.
- Point receivers come from .recp, with the time base taken from pasdetemps rather than from the labels.
- Surface receivers and cutting planes are kept separate by name.
- Particles come from .pbin.
- TCR main results and per-receiver files are read with the 'Global' row separated, and NaN is never averaged.

Our own per-band parameters: SPL, the Schroeder integral, EDT, and T20/T30 by least-squares regression per ISO 3382-1; also C50, C80, D50 and Ts after detecting the direct-sound arrival. Nothing is taken from upstream's GUI or from Night Mode.

Analytic references: Sabine, Eyring with the 4mV term, ISO 9613-1 air attenuation, and the DIN 18041 target.

components.name: core::bed
components.responsibility: Physics beds, run through `cli bed <toml>`. Generates shoebox projects, runs SPPS (computation methods 0 and 1) and TCR, and compares them with the analytic RT. Writes report.json (PASS/FAIL per cell), plus CSV and NPZ decays and PNG plots. The run is single-arm because the solvers are unchanged; any future patch gets the two-arm bed that CLAUDE.md requires.

components.name: cli
components.responsibility: Commands: import, import-proj, check, repair, validate, export-config, mesh, mesh-verify, run, run-folder (a raw folder that bypasses the validator, for negative fixtures), results, bed, and later serve. Every command offers --json and stable exit codes. This is what the gate scripts and CI drive.

components.name: app backend
components.responsibility: Links core. Exposes async commands only, sends run events over an ipc::Channel and datasets as ipc::Response. The only plugins are dialog and, optionally, updater, which is blocked while a run is active. It also provides the --selftest mode (WebGL renderer, IPC benchmark, panic probe) and the e2e test hooks (--open, --project).

components.name: app UI
components.responsibility:
The Concept B chrome and steps: a menu bar with the project as a tab, a step bar with the variant switch, the scene list, the properties panel, and a bottom dock with Acoustics, Console and Runs tabs.

React owns only the chrome, forms, trees and tables. The viewport, console list, uPlot charts and playback clock are imperative islands fed from an external store.

The materials grid is hand-written, with TSV paste and natural band sort. Fonts are bundled locally and the CSP is strict.

components.name: viewport
components.responsibility:
The inside view (BackSide culling, partitions exempt), EdgesGeometry outlines, BVH picking, and an iterative coplanar flood-fill on double-click. Also:
- the plan inset as a scissored viewport in one WebGL context
- surface maps as a faces x steps data texture with the colour map applied in the shader
- particle trajectories held on the GPU and animated by a time uniform on one shared Animator timeline

components.name: oracle
components.responsibility: A probe built from the 9 Boost-free lib_interface files (bin, mbin, poly, gabe, rsbin, part_io, cxml, coreString, pugixml, plus a std::filesystem shim), taken from the archived tag. `oracle dump <file>` prints a canonical text form that is diffed against the Rust decode and against every Rust-written file. Never shipped.

components.name: solvers build
components.responsibility: solvers/build.ps1 runs `git archive 929a5c8` into D:, then configures through a wrapper CMakeLists: upstream cmake/CPM.cmake plus SetupBoost.cmake, then add_subdirectory for lib_interface, spps, ctr and tetgen. It uses the 'Visual Studio 17 2022' generator (this avoids the broken ninja on PATH), x64 Release, with CPM_SOURCE_CACHE on D:. It logs the exact command and writes solvers/manifest.json.

components.name: gates + CI
components.responsibility: One script per milestone, tools/gates/mN.ps1. Each exits 0 only if every listed check passes. CI on windows-latest runs fmt, clippy, the tests and every gate up to the current milestone.

components.name: e2e
components.responsibility: Scripted GUI scenarios for M9 to M13. They check the DOM, the viewport test hooks and tasklist, and compare what the UI shows against the JSON the CLI produces for the same run.

options.name: A. C++ CLI core that links lib_interface, driven by a thin Rust shell over JSON lines
options.shape: A new C++17 executable, core.exe (CMake, MSVC 14.44), statically links all of upstream's lib_interface for the .cbin/.mbin/.poly writers and the GABE/.csbin/.pbin readers. It adds its own config.xml writer, TetGen .node/.ele/.face/.neigh-to-.mbin converter, geometry check and repair, run manager (CreateProcessW plus a Job Object) and parameters. core.exe is also the CLI. The Tauri Rust backend spawns it as a sidecar and speaks JSON lines over stdio. Bulk arrays travel as files in a cache folder. Solvers stay child processes of core.exe.
options.wins_because: [verified] It reuses the most code: Night Mode's harvest files are already C++17. wc gives solver.cpp 2,217 lines, result_parser.cpp 942, ply_loader.cpp 819, project.cpp/.h 856 and scene_model.cpp 118. [verified] Six codecs share byte layouts with the solvers because the solvers are compiled from the same source (contract survey: probe_full round-tripped cube.cbin, cube_mesh.mbin and rs_cut.csbin). The team already knows C++. [verified] lib_interface also builds on Linux and macOS, since upstream ships a Flatpak and a dmg (laydown:175).
options.dies_because: (1) It closes off a commercial version. [verified] lib_interface is GPL-3 (bin.cpp:6-21 header), and linking it makes the core a derivative for good. Night Mode's readers say in their own comments that they mirror upstream (result_parser.cpp:62 'matching original gabe.cpp', :620 'match original rsbin.cpp reader exactly', solver.cpp:338). (2) Linking the library does not make the hard parts correct. [verified] lib_interface has no config.xml writer: CXml is read-only (cxml.h:112-120). It has no TetGen output reader either: a grep of src/lib_interface for LoadEleFile finds 0 hits, and the function exists only in the wx GUI (src/isimpa/3dengine/Core/Objet3D_maillage.cpp:117). Those two stages are where the arc item 12 chain broke. [verified, contract survey] The library's own codecs are defective: CformatBIN::ExportBIN returns true on a failed open; CMBIN writes its header before validating; RSBIN::ImportBIN returns true on a missing file with nodes=8192 and then allocates. (3) It does not isolate crashes. The format code throws const char* and int (part_io.cpp, std_rsbin.cpp) and allocates from unchecked counts. A long-lived core.exe dies on one bad result file and takes the run manager of every in-flight solve with it. The fix, one process per operation, turns the protocol into a job queue. (4) The typed schema lives in C++ and must be mirrored by hand into Rust and TypeScript for the UI, so the copies drift. (5) The Tauri shell is Rust regardless, so the product ends up with three languages. (6) [verified] Night Mode's launcher is Win32 CreateProcessA with a 4,096-char ANSI buffer (solver.cpp:1022-1029) and has to be rewritten anyway. [verified, tauri survey] A sidecar kill is TerminateProcess, which does not kill child processes (Microsoft docs), so core.exe must own a job object or Cancel orphans spps.
options.format_correctness_strategy: Byte layouts come for free for .cbin/.mbin/.poly writing and GABE/.csbin/.pbin reading, because those calls go into the solvers' own source. config.xml and TetGen-to-.mbin still have to be proven by test: upstream's golden fixtures (lib_interface/tests, spps/tests/config.xml) plus solver runs. The lib's missing is_open, version and bounds checks need a validating wrapper around every call.
effort_drivers: Building lib_interface outside upstream's tree: [verified] its CMakeLists is not standalone (it needs the SetupBoost macro and CPM). The full lib needs Boost 1.89, whose 7.4 GB CPM cache is queued for deletion (TO-DELETE-2026-09-08.md).

The schema mirrored by hand from C++ into TypeScript
A Win32 async process layer, job objects and UTF-16 paths written in C++

options.name: B. A Rust core library in one Cargo workspace (core lib, clap CLI, and a Tauri app linking the lib), formats written clean-room from a spec, lib_interface used only as a CI oracle
options.shape: Three crates. `core` (lib): a typed project schema in f64 world metres with stable UUIDs, serde-derived; a config.xml writer generated from those types; .cbin/.mbin/.poly writers; readers for GABE, .csbin, .pbin and TetGen output; geometry check, repair and verify, with meshing behind a `Mesher` trait whose first backend is tetgen.exe; a run manager on tokio::process that puts each solver in a Job Object (KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE), reads stdout and stderr concurrently, flushes partial lines at EOF and classifies every line by content; and our own per-band acoustic parameters. `cli` is clap over core. `app` is the Tauri 2.11.x backend calling core through async commands only, with a Channel for run events and ipc::Response for decoded typed arrays. Solvers stay child processes. `oracle/` is a C++ test tool built from the Boost-free subset of lib_interface, run in CI only and never shipped.
options.wins_because: (1) [verified, tauri survey] The Tauri shell is Rust anyway, so this adds no language beyond what Tauri forces. Rust being absent from Grace is a cost every option pays. (2) One schema drives the config.xml writer, CLI validation (schemars) and the UI's types (ts-rs 12.0.1). That is the laydown's 'settings declared once' made a real typed schema, with no hand-mirrored copy to drift. (3) No lib_interface code runs at runtime, which honours the laydown:169 trap and every other process-killing path the contract survey verified. Parsers are bounds-checked Rust, and a panic inside an async command becomes a JoinError, not a dead window. (4) It keeps the commercial option open. The core is our own copyright if written from the spec rather than transliterated. The solvers and TetGen are executed as separate programs, an aggregate in the FSF FAQ's sense. The Mesher trait lets fTetWild (MPL-2.0) or a WIAS-licensed TetGen replace tetgen.exe. (5) Mac and Linux: Rust and tokio are portable. Job Objects map to Unix process groups. Readers that honour the stored struct lengths cope with the LP64 .pbin layout (56/16/16 against 28/8/16 on Win64, from the contract survey). (6) Headless CI is plain `cargo test`, with no display, no Python and no GL stubs. Night Mode's tests need GL stubs to link (tests/gpu_stubs.cpp).
options.dies_because: (1) Every format is re-implemented, so correctness is proven by test, not inherited. A layout slip the fixtures miss would ship; the oracle below exists to prevent that. (2) Rust is new to the team, which makes human review of core code slower and is a real ongoing cost. (3) The core runs inside the GUI process. [inferred] Its remaining crash routes are panic=abort, an OOM from an allocation that skipped validation, or unsafe Win32 code in the job-object layer. Mitigations: panic=unwind, bounded allocations, and the CLI's future `serve` mode, which keeps option E one step away. (4) [verified] Almost no Night Mode code carries over. What carries over is layout knowledge, the tet-face order b,d,c / c,d,a / a,d,b / b,c,a, CreateBox and the fixtures. Clean-room discipline is required: result_parser.cpp and solver.cpp say in their comments that they mirror upstream GPL code, so they must be read as a spec, never transliterated. Whether that is enough for a closed core is a lawyer's question.
options.format_correctness_strategy: Four layers. (1) Spec: docs/formats, written from the contract survey's format_apis and config_xml tables (layouts, sizes, sentinels, band-by-position mapping). Code is written from it. (2) Golden fixtures: upstream lib_interface/tests (cube.cbin 680 B, cube_mesh.mbin 704 B, rs_cut.csbin 2,908 B, test_import1.poly) and spps/tests/config.xml, a trimmed subset of build-clean/sim_output/spps (valid run), and the broken-hall tcr folder as a negative fixture (skipped.face header '535 1', no .neigh). (3) A differential oracle in CI. [verified] probe_formats.exe compiles from 9 lib_interface sources with no Boost include path or library (scratch libif/build.bat:13; 136,192-byte exe), and it round-tripped the upstream fixtures identically to the full-lib build. CI runs it over every .cbin/.mbin/.poly the Rust writers emit, including property-based random models, and compares its canonical dump with Rust's own reading of every solver output. (4) The solver as final oracle. [verified] SPPS prints 'Xml Property <x> doesn't exist !' for every missing attribute (cxml.cpp:108-117): run_ok printed 0 such lines and run_noeps printed 1, which was the only trace of a missing trans_epsilon. A CI solve of the generated box must show 0 such lines, 0 'lost by meshing' in statsSPPS.gabe, and the expected output files. Only then is a writer change accepted.

options.pick: B. A Rust core library in one Cargo workspace (core lib, clap CLI, and a Tauri app linking the lib), formats written clean-room from a spec, lib_interface used only as a CI oracle
options.pick_reason:
Scores per criterion, 0-10, in the order format correctness / headless CI / laydown traps / crash isolation / commercial option / Mac-Linux / Night Mode harvest / cost (higher is cheaper): A 7/6/5/5/1/5/8/4; B 7/9/9/7/9/8/4/7; C 7/6/1/1/1/5/5/4; D 6/6/5/5/1/4/5/3; E 7/9/9/9/9/8/4/5. Format correctness, traps, isolation and the commercial option carry the most weight. Harvest carries the least, because the harvest survey found the value to be layout knowledge, not code.

Why B wins:
(1) Linking lib_interface does not deliver the correctness its advocates want. [verified] The library has no config.xml writer (cxml.h:112-120) and no TetGen reader (0 hits for LoadEleFile in src/lib_interface; it exists only in the wx GUI, Objet3D_maillage.cpp:117). Those two stages are exactly where arc item 12 failed. Its codecs also carry verified defects: ExportBIN returns true on a failed open, and RSBIN reads garbage from a missing file. So A, C and D keep the licence cost of linking and still hand-write the hard part.
(2) B still gets the solvers' own code as a referee, without shipping it. [verified] The Boost-free probe_formats.exe (9 lib_interface files, no Boost, scratch libif/build.bat:13) round-trips upstream's fixtures. [verified] The solver's 'Xml Property X doesn't exist !' line gives a zero-tolerance config.xml check: 0 lines on run_ok, 1 on run_noeps.
(3) Rust is forced by Tauri anyway, so B is the only option that does not add a language. One serde schema feeds the XML writer, CLI validation and the UI's types.
(4) No lib_interface runs at runtime, which satisfies the binding exit() trap. Clean-room formats plus a Mesher trait keep both the commercial path and a TetGen replacement open.

E scores level with B on the criteria and higher on isolation, but it pays for a second protocol and nested job objects to guard a core that has no known killing path left. B keeps E reachable at low cost: the `cli` crate can grow a `serve` mode if an in-process panic is ever observed.

Conditions on the pick, all unverified until done:
- Install rustup with CARGO_HOME and the target dir on D:.
- Benchmark ipc::Response throughput on Grace before designing the data path. The ~50 MB/s Windows figure is anecdotal.
- Build panic=unwind with bounded allocations.
- Write the codecs from docs/formats, never by transliterating result_parser.cpp or solver.cpp, whose comments say they mirror upstream. Whether that suffices for a closed core is a lawyer's question, not an engineering one.

flaws.flaw: The TCR gates cannot pass as written. M7(d) and M8 require TCR's Sabine and Eyring RT to match 'our analytic values' within 0.5%. TCR hard-codes 0.163 as the constant. The textbook value is 24·ln10/c = 0.1610 at the solver's own c = 343.2 m/s, a 1.24% gap. M7(d) also demands 'no NaN appears in any output', while M2(a) asserts that TCR's Global row is NaN.
flaws.consequence: M7 fails for a reason that is not a defect. By depends_on, M8 and then M9-M13 stall behind it. The alternative is to bend the analytic reference to 0.163, which turns the cross-check into a tautology.
flaws.receipt: [verified] B:\repos\I-Simpa-upstream\src\ctr\TC_CalculationCore.cpp:138,140: `return 0.163 * this->mainData.sceneVolume / (...)`. c = 343.2 comes from the contract survey's probe_full cfg output. M2(a) gate text: 'Global row returned separately as NaN'.

flaws.flaw: The M8 reference is not the exact answer for most of the matrix. The gate requires SPPS T30 within 5% of Eyring in a 6x10x3 m room at uniform alpha up to 0.40. Upstream's own validation deliberately uses a quasi-cubic room, 'as close as possible with the hypothesis of diffuse sound field', and still reports about 2 dB SL deviation between codes. The matrix also leaves particle count, receiver radius, duration and dt unset. The tutorial default of dt = 0.01 s gives about 13 samples across a T30 fit when T is about 0.26 s (alpha 0.4).

items.what: .poly writer (WritePoly): turns the scene triangles into TetGen's input file
items.why: Small, and TetGen accepts its output: in the valid corrected-hall run all 7,860 input triangles came back as boundary faces. It leaves out the two things upstream's writer carries and the rest of the chain needs: a boundary marker per facet and full numeric precision.
defects_vs_upstream_contract: [verified] No facet markers. It writes '<n> 0' plus a bare '1' per facet (:478, :482). Upstream writes '<n> 1' and '1 0 <faceIndex>' (upstream src/lib_interface/input_output/poly/poly.cpp:200-211). Result: every one of the 7,860 rows in build-clean/sim_output/spps/model.1.face has marker -1, so TetGen's output has no link back to the scene faces. The .mbin step has to guess that link from vertex indices (see the ConvertTetGenToMbin item).

[verified] Coordinates are written at the default ostream precision of 6 significant digits (:467). Upstream sets the classic locale and max_digits10 (poly.cpp:179-181). Observed: model.poly line 2 reads '0.815472 -6.50773 1.03437', while the source PLY has '0.815471649 -6.50772619 1.03437471'. The tet nodes (which go into .mbin) and the full-float32 .cbin vertices therefore disagree by up to about 5e-5 m on a 42 m hall. [inferred] With georeferenced coordinates the error grows to metres.
[verified] The stream is never imbued with a locale, so a comma-decimal global locale would corrupt the file. Upstream guards against this with os.imbue(std::locale::classic()).

[verified] The region list is always 0 (:490-491), so fitting zones are never meshed as regions. Upstream emits one region per encumbrance with regionIndex = xmlId (poly.cpp:217-228; Objet3D_maillage.cpp:996-1036).
[verified] Face vertex indices are not validated. The config.xml writer silently skips invalid faces (:262-264) but the .cbin and .poly writers do not, so the three face-index spaces can drift apart.

surveys.summary:
I read Night Mode's project model, solver, mesh-export and result-reader code, the tests, the extraction tool and the committed test hall line by line. I checked each file format against the code the solvers actually run in the pinned upstream: CformatBIN, CMBIN, the GABE and rsbin readers, the particle binary format, the config.xml loaders and SPPS/TCR main(). I also decoded the artefacts on disk and tutorial_2.proj in memory. Nothing was written, built or edited.

**Worth porting: the binary format knowledge.** Night Mode's byte layouts for .cbin, .mbin, GABE and .csbin are correct against upstream. So are the tet-face ordering and the neighbour mapping. The layouts can be ported with added checks: a version field, stream state, and bounds on counts read from the file. The .pbin reader matches too, but only for Windows-built files, because upstream's header fields are platform-sized.

**Port with fixes: the mesh pipeline.**
- The .poly writer must carry per-facet markers and full precision.
- The .mbin conversion must use TetGen's .face markers, not vertex-index matching. It must also refuse to proceed when a boundary face has no marker: that face-level condition is what makes SPPS lose particles. It needs a hash tying each .mbin to its .cbin.
- TetGen's exit 3 and its `_skipped.face` file must be treated as failure.
- The config.xml writer can keep its attribute mapping, but it has to become a typed schema.

**Four solve-changing config and model defects, all found in the code:**
- The reflection-law codes are rotated: choosing "Lambert" in the UI sends specular reflection.
- The "Global Power" control never reaches the solver.
- Background noise is written to an element no solver reads, and every receiver is sent 0 dB instead.
- Fitting zones collide with the region attribute 1 that TetGen stamps on every tet, so one fitting zone would take over the whole hall. I traced this through the code but have not run it.

**Rebuild: the run manager.** SPPS always exits 0: its main() ignores the solver's own result. The particle-loss warning is lost too. It is printed last, to stderr, with no newline. RunSolver merges stderr into the same pipe but has no final flush, so that unterminated line is dropped. RunSolver also clears every earlier pipeline warning on entry. That corrects arc item 12's "reads only stdout": stderr is read, and the warning is lost to the missing flush and the clearing. The machine-readable loss record in statsSPPS.gabe is never read. Even the "valid" corrected-hall run loses 30-54 particles per 100,000 per band, below SPPS's 5% print threshold.

**Drop:**
- all the acoustic parameter code: a 26 dB offset in the .gap echogram, NaN reverberation times from TCR, a 3 dB double count at TCR receivers, and broadband instead of per-band parameters
- the .proj loader: it misreads the 32-byte face records and the position elements
- Night Mode's own project save format
- the preprocess call, which is fed a .cbin the tool cannot read
- the 3DS loader, miniz and the GPU code

**Test assets.** The committed `elmia_corrected.ply` is watertight and meshes cleanly, but 31% of its faces are in the wrong group. The extraction tool claims the group split was lost; it is in tutorial_2.proj's `.finfo` files, together with a material id per group. Regenerate the hall from those. The best reference assets are:
- upstream's golden files in `lib_interface/tests` and `spps/tests/config.xml`
- tutorial_2.proj
- the build-clean spps run as format fixtures (its acoustic values are not quotable)
- the broken-hall tcr and mesh folders as negative fixtures

**Verified versus inferred.** Everything is tagged [verified] (from code plus decoded files) or [inferred]. Inferred items:
- the whole-hall fitting zone effect
- the stale-mesh consequence in the UI
- STL welding leading to particle loss
- the 3DS transform effect
- the uint16 time-step overflow
- whether the unlinked surface receivers explain arc item 8

No solver was run for this map. The only run evidence is the existing `build-clean/sim_output` artefacts.

surveys.lib_interface_standalone_build: YES, with conditions. Verified by building it, not only by reading the source. Two throwaway builds were made in %TEMP% (scratch\libif, 5.8 s for both, MSVC 2022 x64 /MD /std:c++17). (A) probe_full.exe is a new CLI linked against the existing Release lib_interface.lib. That lib is 10,622,456 bytes and was built from the pinned tag at B:\repos\I-Simpa-upstream\build_solvers\src\lib_interface\Release\. The link also needs libboost_filesystem-vc143-mt-x64-1_89.lib (plus atomic). It linked and round-tripped upstream's own fixtures: cube.cbin with 8 vertices and 12 faces, cube_mesh.mbin with 6 tetrahedra and volume 125.000 m3, and rs_cut.csbin with 30 nodes, 1 receiver and 5 time steps. (B) probe_formats.exe was compiled from the format sources alone: bin.cpp, mbin.cpp, poly.cpp, gabe.cpp, rsbin.cpp, part_io.cpp, cxml.cpp, coreString.cpp and pugixml.cpp, plus a 7-line std::filesystem replacement for std_tools.cpp. It used NO Boost include path and NO Boost library, and gave identical results. Conclusions: (1) The format layer is Boost-free. Boost is needed only by the solver-side files: std_tools.cpp (filesystem), baseReportManager.cpp (filesystem::exists) and directivityParser.cpp (algorithm/string plus header-only regex). Base_Core_Configuration pulls in directivityParser, so reading config.xml the way the solver does needs Boost; CXml alone does not. (2) src/lib_interface/CMakeLists.txt does not stand alone. It calls SetupBoost(), a macro from the top-level cmake/SetupBoost.cmake that also needs CPM. It uses a directory-scoped include_directories(.), so consumers must add src/lib_interface themselves, as spps/CMakeLists.txt:10 does. A standalone CMake wrapper of the full lib was NOT built; that part is inferred to be trivial. (3) exit() survivability in a separate process HOLDS for the parent, and this was verified. probe_full called initMesh on a config missing material 7. The child printed the stderr message and exited -1 (0xFFFFFFFF), and the calling process continued. But it only matters on the solver-init path: the only exit() calls in lib_interface are coreTypes.cpp:215 (t_TetraMesh::LoadFile) and coreinitialisation.cpp:431 (initMesh; the laydown says 432). No format API calls exit(). The format APIs have other ways to kill a process, and these are just as fatal in-process. RSBIN::ImportBIN on a missing file returns TRUE with garbage sizes (verified: nodes=8192, nbTimeStep=4096) and then new[]s them. part_io, std_rsbin and mathlib throw const char* or int. GABE SetString strcpys into 50 bytes (gabe.cpp:177). Indices are unchecked. So the process boundary should be one process per operation, never a long-lived core that has lib_interface linked in. Or lib_interface should serve as a reference oracle in CI and not as a runtime dependency (recommendation; inference).

WORKING DIRECTORY AND PATHS
- Every file is wd + name, where wd = configuration@workingdirectory, concatenated raw. It must be absolute with a trailing separator (sppsNantes.cpp:300-302; main_tc.cpp:66-68).
- No file is read or written relative to the process cwd when wd is absolute (VERIFIED: the cwd_* folders stayed empty in every run).
- The config path argument is opened through a narrow (ANSI) API. A folder name outside CP1252 ('Ł') fails silently with exit 0 (VERIFIED). Workaround, VERIFIED: cwd = the run folder, argument 'config.xml', wd = absolute UTF-8 path.

findings.answer: VERIFIED: Sidecars are listed in `bundle.externalBin`. Each file needs a target-triple suffix, for example spps-x86_64-pc-windows-msvc.exe. They are spawned with `app.shell().sidecar(name).spawn()`, which returns `(rx, child)` with CommandEvent::{Stdout(Vec<u8>), Stderr(Vec<u8>), Error, Terminated}. Output handling: (1) by default the plugin splits output on '\n' OR '\r'. `set_raw_out` switches this off. A final line with no newline is still emitted at EOF. (2) The event channel is `channel(1)`, which means backpressure, not data loss. (3) On Windows the plugin sets CREATE_NO_WINDOW. (4) Kill path: `CommandChild::kill` calls shared_child's kill, which calls std `Child::kill`, which calls `TerminateProcess(handle, 1)`. Microsoft: 'When the system is terminating a process, it does not terminate any child processes that the process has created.' So if our core CLI runs as a sidecar and itself launches spps.exe or tetgen.exe, Cancel kills the core and orphans the solver. This is the same bug as upstream issues #69/#181. Solver facts from upstream source: SPPS writes progress as `#<pct>` plus endl on stdout (lib_interface/input_output/progressionInfo.h:154-155). The particle-loss warning goes to stderr through fprintf WITHOUT a trailing newline (src/spps/sppsNantes.cpp:438). 'Unable to find the source position!' goes to stderr, also with no newline (sppsNantes.cpp:63). RECOMMENDED (inferred): run the solvers from our Rust core with tokio::process, not through the JS-facing shell plugin. Put every solver in a Windows Job Object with JOB_OBJECT_LIMIT_KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE, so that Cancel, an app crash or quitting kills the whole tree. Read stdout and stderr concurrently and tag each line with its stream and a timestamp. Flush partial lines at EOF. Classify each line by content, not by stream or exit code. Record 'cancelled' explicitly, because TerminateProcess leaves exit code 1, which reads like an ordinary failure, and upstream counts only negative codes as failure. Stream the classified lines to the UI over a tauri::ipc::Channel, batched roughly every 50 ms.

findings.topic: Moving large binary data Rust -> UI: IPC throughput on Windows
findings.answer: VERIFIED: The event system 'is not designed for low latency or high throughput'. Channels 'are designed to be fast and deliver ordered data'. `tauri::ipc::Response::new(Vec<u8>)` returns raw bytes with no JSON step, and channels can carry raw bytes too. Below 8192 B of JSON or 1024 B of raw data, payloads go through eval. Anything larger is queued and fetched over the IPC custom protocol. On Windows, custom protocols are built on WebView2 AddWebResourceRequestedFilter at http://<scheme>.localhost. Wry wraps each response body in SHCreateMemStream, a full copy, and dispatches the handler onto the UI thread. Microsoft says WebResourceRequested is 'raised on the WebView2 UI thread of your host app process' and is slower than file URLs or virtual-host mapping. The only public figure is a maintainer-relayed, 'non-scientific' benchmark from Dec 2024: 10 MB took about 200 ms on Windows against about 5 ms on macOS, roughly 50 MB/s. Our real payloads, measured on the corrected Elmia solve: each Surface_receiver rs_cut.csbin is 13.5-13.7 MB per band and 16.5 MB for Global, 98.4 MB for all 7. Each particles.pbin is 3.18 MB per band at 500 rendered particles x 400 steps, from config nbparticules_rendu=500, duree 2 s, pasdetemps 0.005. INFERRED: At about 50 MB/s, one band's surface map costs about 0.3 s and all bands about 2 s. That is fine for load-on-select and fatal for per-frame streaming. Large transfers also run on the UI thread, so window drag and resize will stutter while they happen. Design rules: (1) never send per-frame data. The core decodes solver files once into GPU-ready typed arrays (float32 or half-float, face-indexed), and the GPU animates them with a time uniform. (2) Start with raw `Response` per dataset, plus a progress Channel. (3) Benchmark on Grace before building anything cleverer. If users raise the rendered-particle count, a 10k-particle band is about 64 MB and needs one of the alternatives below.

findings.topic: Large-data alternatives: custom protocol, asset protocol, virtual host, shared buffer
findings.answer: VERIFIED: (a) `register_asynchronous_uri_scheme_protocol` gives HTTP semantics such as Range and caching, but on Windows it runs through the same WebResourceRequested and UI-thread path as IPC. A 2024 comment reports that WebView2 custom protocols do not support streaming. (b) The asset protocol (`convertFileSrc`) must be enabled, scoped and allowed in the CSP. It is also a custom scheme at http://asset.localhost. (c) WebView2 virtual host mapping (`SetVirtualHostNameToFolderMapping`, ICoreWebView2_3) is resolved inside the WebView2 processes, which Microsoft calls 'a faster option than WebResourceRequested'. Tauri 2 exposes the WebView2 controller and environment through `webview.with_webview(|w| w.controller())`. (d) `PostSharedBufferToScript` (ICoreWebView2_17, runtime 1.0.1661.34 or later) hands the page a zero-copy ArrayBuffer through the chrome.webview 'sharedbufferreceived' event. INFERRED: The best fallback is (c). The core writes each decoded dataset as a static binary cache under app_cache_dir/<run-id>/, the app maps a virtual host to that folder only, and the frontend fetch()es the file. Its costs: Windows-only unsafe webview2-com code, a v3 migration touch-point (with_webview moves to WebviewWryExt), and a folder-scoped exposure that must stay narrow. Keep (d) in reserve. A search summary of the 2022 IPC discussion says users found WebView2 shared memory 'weirdly slow'. I did not quote that from the thread, so treat it as unconfirmed. Do not use (a) or (b) for speed, because on Windows they gain nothing over raw IPC.

findings.topic: 3D in WebView2: three.js, WebGL2/WebGPU, picking, performance ceilings
findings.answer: VERIFIED: three.js r186 was released 2026-09-08 under MIT. It exports both 'three' (WebGLRenderer, WebGL2) and 'three/webgpu'. WebGPURenderer falls back to its WebGL2 backend automatically and has `forceWebGL`. WebView2 supports WebGL2 per caniwebview; its WebGPU row is only asterisked. Grace has WebView2 Runtime 153.0.4234.48 and one GPU, the RTX 5070 (driver 32.0.15.9636). In three.js, `linewidth` is ignored by WebGL and WebGPU, so lines are always 1 px. EdgesGeometry(thresholdAngle) draws only the edges where adjacent face normals differ by more than the threshold, which implements the laydown's 'outline wireframe instead of every triangle edge'. three-mesh-bvh v0.9.15 (MIT, 2026-09-09) claims 500 rays against an 80,000-polygon model at 60 fps. INFERRED: A room of about 10k faces is trivial for any GPU from the last decade. The ceilings that matter come from data volume, not triangle count. Use WebGLRenderer on WebGL2 as the baseline. WebGPU is not needed at this scale, and in WebView2 it is unverified. Map the design to three.js as follows: 'inside view' is material.side = BackSide with partitions exempt. Outlines are EdgesGeometry plus Line2/LineMaterial fat lines. Picking is three-mesh-bvh raycasts for hover and click. Coplanar flood-fill should be an iterative BFS over a face-adjacency table built once in the core. Particles: pack trajectories (x,y,z,energy per step, variable first step) into a float texture or storage buffer and animate with a time uniform. 500 x 400 steps is 3.2 MB and trivial. At about 10k particles, 64 MB per band, window by time. Surface maps: store a faces x timesteps scalar texture and apply the black-red-yellow colour map in the shader. Draw the plan-view inset as a second scissored viewport in the SAME canvas and WebGL context, not as a second canvas.

findings.topic: Frontend stack: framework choice for a dense pro-tool UI
findings.answer: RECOMMENDATION: React 19 (19.3.0) + TypeScript + Vite (8.3.0), with one hard rule. React owns only the chrome, forms, trees and tables. Everything hot is an imperative island fed from a store outside React: the three.js viewport, the console list, the uPlot charts and the playback clock. Reasons, with receipts: (1) Tauri needs an SPA, SSG or MPA and names Vite as the SPA path. (2) The approved design's logic is a class component with this.state, setState and componentWillUnmount (concept-b-approved.dc.html, DCLogic block), so porting it to React is mechanical. (3) The pro-tool widgets that exist target React. dockview 8.3.1 (MIT) supports React, Vue, Angular and vanilla but not Svelte. Glide Data Grid (MIT, canvas) is React-only. (4) Traps to avoid: AG Grid's range selection and clipboard are Enterprise, meaning commercial, and Handsontable is not free for commercial use and not open source, so neither suits a GPL app that might later go commercial. Hand-write the materials table instead. It is about 20 rows x 6-8 bands, and TSV paste, fill and natural sort cost a few hundred lines. (5) Use uPlot (MIT, about 50 KB, 166k points in 25 ms) for RT and decay charts. INFERRED trade-off: Svelte 5 (5.57.1) or Solid (1.9.15) would give fine-grained updates for free. findings.topic: Security and capabilities for process spawning
findings.answer: VERIFIED: Shell plugin commands such as execute, spawn, kill and stdin-write are blocked by default. JS-side sidecar use needs `shell:allow-spawn` with `sidecar: true` and, optionally, regex validators for the arguments. INFERRED: If only the Rust core spawns solvers, the webview gets no shell permission at all. The frontend calls typed commands like run_simulation(project_id), and the core builds the argument list itself, which removes argument-injection paths such as receiver labels reaching folder names or printf. Those are laydown traps, and the core must still sanitise labels.

findings.topic: GPL-3 implications of bundling GPL/AGPL solver executables in a Tauri installer
findings.answer: VERIFIED: Shipping separate programs together is an 'aggregate', permitted even when the licences differ. Putting them in one container, such as an installer, does not change that analysis (FSF FAQ #MereAggregation, #AggregateContainers). 'pipes, sockets and command-line arguments are communication mechanisms normally used between two separate programs', with the caveat that communication 'intimate enough, exchanging complex internal data structures' could make them one program. AGPLv3 and GPLv3 explicitly permit combination (#AGPLGPL). AGPL §13's network clause applies only to programs 'expressly designed to accept user requests and send responses over a network' (#AGPLv3InteractingRemotely). Apache-2.0, one of Tauri's licences, is GPLv3-compatible. three.js, three-mesh-bvh, uPlot, React and dockview are MIT. GPL-3 §1 'System Libraries' covers components of a 'compiler used to produce the work', which is the usual basis for shipping the MSVC runtime. TetGen is AGPL-3 or a paid WIAS licence. INFERRED obligations for the GPL-3 release: include LICENSE, THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES and the TetGen licence text, and publish Corresponding Source for every shipped binary. For solvers that means the pinned tag 929a5c8, our patches/, and the exact build scripts and flags, for example the static-CRT flags if used, attached to the same GitHub release as the installer. For a desktop app, AGPL §13 does not trigger. It WOULD trigger for a future hosted or cloud version running a modified TetGen.

findings.topic: Keeping a future commercial version possible
findings.answer: VERIFIED: The FSF says GPL programs can ship 'alongside' a proprietary system if they 'communicate at arms length' (#GPLInProprietarySystem). Night Mode's readers are explicitly derived from upstream GPL code: result_parser.cpp:620 says 'match original rsbin.cpp reader exactly', line 62 says 'matching original gabe.cpp ReadFile methods', and solver.cpp:338 says 'Types matching I-Simpa's bin.cpp'. fTetWild is MPL-2.0. INFERRED: GPL-3 now does not foreclose commercial later IF: (1) the core and GUI talk to solvers only through exec, config.xml and files, never linking solver or lib_interface code. (2) Format readers and writers in the new core are written from a written format spec (clean-room). Code copied or ported line-by-line from upstream, or from those Night Mode functions, makes the core a GPL derivative for good. (3) All new-repo code is owned by Burhan and Michael, with a contributor agreement before any outside PR is merged, so they can dual-license. (4) TetGen, used for meshing, needs the WIAS licence or a replacement for a closed build. fTetWild (MPL-2.0) is one candidate whose output SPPS compatibility has not been examined. The 'intimate data structures' caveat on the solver boundary is a question for a lawyer, not for engineering.
